about: The keys of a simplified policy's predicates object, beside predicates.mongodbPredicate, which access-control 6.1.6 needs to accept predicates (round 42: r42open-predicates-nested-*). The policy has no condition, so check/resource allows; the filter says which keys became predicates of which dialect.

cases.about: Control: a DENY rule over a resource attribute that does not hold. True unless the stand answers every check with 400.

A top-level rsqlPredicate a==top, and inside predicates a mongodbPredicate, an rsqlPredicate a==nested and a sqlPredicate. r42open-predicates-nested-every-format showed the nested rsql and sql keys ignored beside mongodbPredicate when no top-level key is set; this case is a second carrier for that. Round 42 asked a top-level and a nested rsqlPredicate together only without mongodbPredicate, and the upload was refused. Expected: the rsql text a==top and the mongodb text only. An rsql a==nested means the nested rsqlPredicate counts over the top-level one; a sql text, that the nested sqlPredicate counts.
Control: a DENY rule over a resource attribute that does not hold. True unless the stand answers every check with 400.
